draft.title: Australia's health care system
card: Medicare
Australia's public health insurance scheme, paid for by the government. It funds care in public hospitals and subsidises part of the cost of visits to doctors.
PBS
The Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme. It subsidises the price of many prescription medicines, so patients pay less than the full cost.
Private health insurance
People can choose to buy it. It adds choice, such as picking a doctor or a private hospital, and it works alongside Medicare.
A subsidy is money the government pays toward a cost. It lowers what the patient pays but may not cover all of it.
draft.remember: Medicare covers hospitals and doctors, the PBS covers medicines, and private insurance adds choice.

a.q: Which part of the system lowers the price a patient pays for a prescription medicine?
opts: The Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme
Medicare funding of public hospitals
Private hospital cover only
A subsidy on doctor visits
a.why: The PBS subsidises the price of many prescription medicines. Medicare subsidises doctor visits and funds public hospital care, so it is not the scheme that lowers medicine prices.
a.clue: Think of the scheme named for medicines.

b.q: Tariq is treated in a public hospital after a fall. He then buys a medicine on prescription. Which scheme funds each?
opts: Medicare funds the hospital, the PBS subsidises the medicine
The PBS funds the hospital, Medicare subsidises the medicine
Private insurance funds the hospital, the PBS the medicine
Medicare funds both the hospital and the medicine
b.why: Medicare funds public hospital care, and the PBS subsidises medicines. The last option is tempting because Medicare is the main public scheme, but the medicine subsidy comes from the PBS.
b.clue: Match each cost to the scheme set up for it.

b.best: Medicare funds the hospital, the PBS subsidises the medicine

problems.detail: The remember line says Medicare 'covers hospitals and doctors' and the PBS 'covers medicines'. The card is narrower: Medicare funds public hospital care and subsidises only part of doctor visits, and the PBS subsidises many prescription medicines. 'Covers' suggests full payment, which goes against the card's own point that a subsidy may not cover all of the cost.
The clue 'Think of the scheme named for medicines' all but names the answer, since only one option is a scheme named for medicines. A student can pick it without knowing what the PBS does.

The stem asks 'Which scheme funds each?', but the PBS subsidises medicines rather than funding them in full. The right option itself says 'subsidises', so the stem slightly blurs the funding-versus-subsidy distinction the card teaches.

check.summary: The facts and both intended answers are correct. The remember line overstates the card by saying Medicare and the PBS 'cover' costs they only subsidise, the clue for question a nearly gives the answer away, and question b's stem blurs funding with subsidising.
